head: 0098ee939e2d701ca3085c9e8e2fe3003a907836
summary:
The M2 fix (O-020) is correct and tested. But the enumeration the builder asked for turned up one more major gap (M3) and one minor one (m1), filed together so this does not cost another lap per shape.

**The fix.** `eng/rules-parity.ps1:192-194` now refuses any dash at column 0 to 2 that does not carry `name:` on the same line (`^ {0,2}-(\s|$)`), and list items at 4 or 6 spaces never match it. C-005 in `tests/rules/RuleCases.ps1:367-382` feeds a bare-dash entry first after `rules:`, one just above the settled marker, and one at column 0. Each must give CANNOT-READ at its dash line. I read those rows and they feed the shape in.

**What I re-ran on this tree:**
- RuleCases C-001 to C-005: 8, 34, 26, 26 and 102 checks, none failing, under both powershell.exe and pwsh.
- RuleCopiesAgreeTests plus ArchitectureRulesTests: 8/8.
- The full harness against the real engine: CLEAN, 32/32 rows AS-RECORDED, exit 0. That makes six runs with the same verdict for every row.
- `git status` was unchanged afterwards.

**The enumeration.** I tried the YAML spellings the builder named, plus others, each on a temp copy checked against the engine's own loader (it opens the file with `open(path, encoding='utf-8')` then calls `yaml.safe_load`, at `taad3/fitness.py:301-302`).

These are refused, or break Fitness loudly:

| Spelling | Parity | Fitness |
|---|---|---|
| Flow-mapping entry | CANNOT-READ | — |
| `? name` complex key | CANNOT-READ | — |
| Anchored `- &e` entry | CANNOT-READ | — |
| Flow list of patterns | CANNOT-READ | — |
| Tab-indented item | DRIFT | ScannerError |
| Column-0 key with a scalar value | — | ParserError |

These still give AGREE while the engine reads something else:
- **M3 (major):** a second column-0 key after `rules:`. A duplicate `rules:` leaves Fitness with 1 rule. A key such as `parked:` moves 8 rules out of the list Fitness reads.
- **m1 (minor):** line breaks other than LF or CRLF (a lone CR, U+0085, U+2028) hide a whole yaml-only entry inside what the reader takes for one line.

The harness's clean check, which compares Fitness's rule count with twinned plus settled entries, would catch both where the engine exists. RuleCopiesAgreeTests, the routine gate, does not.

**Stale statements.** Nothing in the files I passed now describes old behaviour falsely. The C-005 title and the new comments are accurate.

findings.claim: A column-0 key after `rules:` changes which entries PyYAML, and so Fitness, reads as the rules list, and the parity reader neither sees nor refuses it. The reader takes the first `^rules:\s*$` line and scans every later line for entries, ignoring any other column-0 line. Two cases, both checked on a temp copy against yaml.safe_load, the engine's loader. (a) A second `rules:` block appended at the end with one entry gave 'rules-parity: AGREE 7 facts <- 10 twinned entries, 21 patterns; 8 settled entries not compared', exit 0. safe_load keeps the last duplicate key, so Fitness's list holds 1 rule and none of the 10 twinned entries is enforced. (b) A bare `parked:` line at column 0, inserted before the TheScannerMakesNoBclFileSystemCalls entry, also gave AGREE with 10 twinned entries, exit 0. safe_load then gives rules = 9 and parked = 8, so that twin and all 7 settled rules drop out of Fitness. The engine does not refuse either case: taad3/fitness.py:306-313 checks only that `rules` exists and is a list. The header's authoring rule ('`rules:` stays the only top-level key and the last thing in the file', .taad/fitness.yaml:69-70) is therefore enforced by nothing. RuleCopiesAgreeTests stays green while Fitness has quietly stopped enforcing rules xUnit still enforces. This is the class of M1 and M2: a shape the reader neither reads the way YAML does nor refuses.
findings.evidence: eng/rules-parity.ps1:178-194 (Read-Entries): line 180 takes the first `^rules:\s*$`; the scan at 187-195 only reacts to `- name:` and `^ {0,2}-(\s|$)` lines, so a column-0 `rules:` or `parked:` line passes unremarked. The engine's side: taad3/fitness.py:301-313 in the taad_v3 checkout.
findings.fix: In Read-Entries, after the `rules:` line, refuse (Stop-Reading with file:line) any line that is non-blank, starts at column 0 and is not a comment: `$lines[$i] -cmatch '^[^\s#]'`. Do this before the dash checks, or keep the bare-dash message by checking dashes first. That refuses a duplicate `rules:`, any other top-level key, and `---`/`...` markers. Then add C-005 rows for a duplicate `rules:` block at the end and a column-0 key between twinned entries, each requiring CANNOT-READ under powershell.exe and pwsh.

findings.claim: Read-Lines splits the rule files on `\r?\n` only. The engine opens fitness.yaml in Python text mode, where universal newlines turn a lone CR into a line break, and PyYAML also breaks lines at U+0085, U+2028 and U+2029. So a whole entry can sit inside what the reader treats as one line. Checked on a temp copy: appending `<sep>  - name: 'Hidden (*.cs)'<sep>    files: 'src/**/*.cs'<sep>    must_not_match:<sep>      - '(?m)OnlyInYaml'` to the NoBcl entry's `    including_comments: true` line gave 'rules-parity: AGREE 7 facts <- 10 twinned entries, 21 patterns', exit 0. That held for <sep> = lone CR, U+0085 and U+2028, while an engine-style `open()` plus safe_load read 18 rules including 'Hidden (*.cs)'. This is minor because normal editing on this platform does not produce these characters. The C# side is covered already: a lone CR there breaks the lone-literal regex, and the reflected Fact count backs the Fact reader.
findings.evidence: eng/rules-parity.ps1:60-66, Read-Lines: `return , ($text -split "`r?`n")`. Engine: taad3/fitness.py:301 `open(path, encoding="utf-8")` then `yaml.safe_load`.
findings.fix: In Read-Lines, refuse (Stop-Reading with file:line) any text containing a CR not followed by LF, U+0085, U+2028 or U+2029. Alternatively, split on `\r\n|[\r\n\u0085  ]` so the reader breaks lines where YAML does. Add a C-005 row with a lone-CR-separated hidden entry that must not give AGREE.

drift: Nothing new departed from the design in attempt 3. The entry refusal is wider than the reviewer's suggested fix, `^ {0,2}-(\s|$)` instead of `^  -(\s|$)`, because the M2 decision chose it. The message now reads "an entry that does not start with 'name:' on its dash line".

Parity compares must_not_match patterns only. A twinned entry that gains a `must_not_import:` key, which Fitness enforces and xUnit has no twin for, reads AGREE. This is the same declared blind spot as scopes, exemptions and including_comments, and the harness catches it only if the clean tree violates the new import rule. It is recorded here so the design's 'patterns only' scope is read as covering must_not_import too.
